claims.evidence: Co-localization quantification validating NICD1 as marker of Notch activity.

claims.claim: Mice lacking Lfng have markedly fewer NSCs than wild-type mice.
claims.source: Mice lacking Lfng had markedly fewer NSCs than wild-type mice (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: Quantification of NSC numbers in constitutive knockout mice.

claims.claim: NSCs lacking Lfng are cycling (Ki67+) in significantly higher proportions than wild-type NSCs (p=0.0221).
claims.source: We examined the ratio of cycling Ki67+ NSCs and BrdU+ NSCs in mutant and wild-type mice and found that NSCs lacking Lfng were both cycling (Figure 5C, left panel) and in S-phase (Figure 5C, middle panel) in significantly higher proportions than wild-type NSCs (N = 4; p=0.0221 for Ki67+ NSCs; p=0.0017 for BrdU+ NSCs).
claims.evidence: Quantification of cell cycle markers in knockout versus wild-type mice.

claims.claim: NSCs lacking Lfng are in S-phase (BrdU+) in significantly higher proportions than wild-type NSCs (p=0.0017).
claims.source: We examined the ratio of cycling Ki67+ NSCs and BrdU+ NSCs in mutant and wild-type mice and found that NSCs lacking Lfng were both cycling (Figure 5C, left panel) and in S-phase (Figure 5C, middle panel) in significantly higher proportions than wild-type NSCs (N = 4; p=0.0221 for Ki67+ NSCs; p=0.0017 for BrdU+ NSCs).
claims.evidence: Quantification of S-phase entry in knockout versus wild-type mice.

claims.claim: Considerably more mutant NSCs are in S-phase than either wild-type NSC clones or NSCs in control mice in iLfngfl/fl conditional knockout mice.
claims.source: Considerably more mutant NSCs were in S-phase than were either wild-type NSC clones or NSCs in control mice (Figure 5C, right panel).
claims.evidence: Quantification of BrdU incorporation in conditional knockout clones versus controls.

claims.claim: iLfngfl/fl wild-type clones have a similar ratio of BrdU+ NSCs as control mice.
claims.source: Interestingly, iLfngfl/fl wild-type clones had a similar ratio of BrdU+ NSCs as control mice (Figure 5C, right panel), suggesting that the effect of Lfng in NSCs is cell-autonomous.
claims.evidence: Comparison of BrdU incorporation between non-recombined clones and controls, leading to inference about cell autonomy.

claims.claim: When Lfng−/+ mice are subjected to ECS, they have a significantly higher ratio of BrdU+ NSCs than observed in either sham Lfng−/+ control (p=0.0178) or ECS-treated Lfng-eGFP mice.
claims.source: This effect persists not only in physiological but also in pathological conditions: when Lfng−/+ mice were subjected to ECS, they had a significantly higher ratio of BrdU+ NSCs than observed in either sham Lfng−/+ control (N = 3–4, p=0.0178; Figure 5D) or ECS-treated Lfng-eGFP mice (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: Comparison of ECS response in knockout versus control mice.

claims.claim: Notch signaling, as measured by NICD1 immunofluorescence intensity, is much lower in individual mutant NSC clones in iLfngfl/fl mice two weeks after induction compared to controls.
claims.source: Indeed, Notch signaling, as measured by NICD1 immunofluorescence intensity, was much lower in individual mutant NSC clones in iLfngfl/fl mice two weeks after induction compared to controls (Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: Quantification of NICD1 intensity in mutant versus control NSCs.

claims.claim: Many double-labeled NSCs (CldU/IdU) are observed in wild-type mice at 3 and 7 days, but only a few are detected in Lfng−/+ mice at either timepoint, and none are found in iLfngfl/fl mice.
claims.source: Many double-labeled NSCs were observed in the wild-type mice, only a few were detected in the Lfng−/+ mice at either timepoint, but none were found in iLfngfl/fl mice (Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: Sequential thymidine analog labeling showing differences in cell cycle re-entry.

claims.claim: Lfng−/+ mice have a decreased ratio of CldU/Ki67 double labeled NSCs 7 days following CldU injection (p=0.0105).
claims.source: As Lfng−/+ mice had a decreased ratio of CldU/Ki67 double labeled NSCs 7 days following CldU injection (N = 4; p=0.0105; Figure 5G), these data strongly indicate that Lfng mutant NSCs either dilute BrdU by multiple divisions, die, or directly differentiate/ transform into another cell type over the course of seven days.
claims.evidence: Quantification of cycling NSCs retaining label, leading to inference about cell fate.

claims.claim: In Lfng mutant mice, after a two-hour pulse, only 5.2% of the initial BrdU+ NSC population retains BrdU after 7 days (p=0.0003).
claims.source: In Lfng mutant mice, after a two-hour pulse, only 5.2% of the initial BrdU+ NSC population retained BrdU after 7 days (N = 4 per timepoint, p=0.0003).
claims.evidence: BrdU retention assay showing loss of label in mutant NSCs.

claims.claim: In control mice, 92.4% of the initial BrdU+ NSC population retains BrdU after 7 days (p=0.38).
claims.source: In control mice, however, 92.4% of the initial BrdU+ NSC population retained BrdU after 7 days (N = 4 per timepoint, p=0.38).
claims.evidence: BrdU retention assay showing maintenance of label in control NSCs.

claims.claim: iLfngfl/fl mice have fewer apoptotic cells than control mice.
claims.source: Both immunostaining for activated caspase-3 and the ApopTag assay, which detects DNA strand breaks, indicated that iLfngfl/fl actually had fewer apoptotic cells than control (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: Apoptosis detection assays showing reduced cell death in mutants.

claims.claim: There is a declining trend in the number of mutant NSCs at 1, 7, and 30 days post-induction in iLfngfl/fl mice (p=0.8215; 0.11; 0.06 for 1, 7, and 30 days, respectively).
claims.source: We observed a declining trend in the number of mutant NSCs (p=0.8215; 0.11; 0.06 for 1, 7, and 30 days, respectively), and a significant decline in the number of mutant ANPs (p=0.2817; 0.0024; 0.0049 for 1, 7, and 30 days, respectively) (Figure 5H, middle panel).
claims.evidence: Longitudinal quantification of cell populations in conditional knockout.

claims.claim: There is a significant decline in the number of mutant ANPs at 7 and 30 days post-induction in iLfngfl/fl mice (p=0.0024; 0.0049 for 7 and 30 days, respectively).
claims.source: We observed a declining trend in the number of mutant NSCs (p=0.8215; 0.11; 0.06 for 1, 7, and 30 days, respectively), and a significant decline in the number of mutant ANPs (p=0.2817; 0.0024; 0.0049 for 1, 7, and 30 days, respectively) (Figure 5H, middle panel).
claims.evidence: Longitudinal quantification showing reduced ANP production in mutants.

claims.claim: There is a notable increase in tdTomato+ astrocyte-like cells at 7 and 30 days post-induction in iLfngfl/fl mice (p=0.0003 and p<0.0001, respectively).
claims.source: Interestingly, we observed a notable increase in tdTomato+ astrocyte-like cells at 7 and 30 days post-induction (p=0.0003 and p<0.0001, respectively).
claims.evidence: Quantification showing increased astrocytic differentiation in mutants.

claims.claim: A greater number of BrdU-retaining astrocyte-like cells are found in Lfng mutant mice at 7 days (p=0.0302) but not at 30 days (p=0.4412).
claims.source: we quantified the BrdU-retaining astrocyte-like cells and found a greater number of these cells in Lfng mutant mice, but only at 7 days (N = 4 per group, p=0.0302; Figure 5H, right panel). At 30 days, there was no difference compared to control mice (p=0.4412), suggesting that NSCs lacking Lfng differentiate more rapidly into astrocyte-like cells, depleting the NSC population more quickly.
claims.evidence: BrdU retention assay showing temporal dynamics of astrocytic differentiation, leading to inference about differentiation rate.

claims.claim: Mice lacking Dll1 have far fewer NSCs than wild-type mice or those lacking Jag1.
claims.source: Mice lacking Dll1 (Dll1tm1Gos (JAX 002957; Dll1−/+)) (Hrabĕĕ de Angelis et al., 1997) had far fewer NSCs than wild-type mice or those lacking Jag1 (Jag1tm1Grid (JAX 010616; Jag1−/+)) (Xue et al., 1999) or Lfng (Figure 6A, Figure 5B, respectively).
claims.evidence: Quantification of NSC numbers in Dll1 knockout mice compared to other genotypes, with citations.

claims.claim: Dll1−/+ mice have a substantial increase in the ratio of cycling Ki67+ cells (p=0.0007) and BrdU+ NSCs (p<0.0001).
claims.source: This was accompanied by a substantial increase in the ratio of cycling, Ki67+ cells and BrdU+ NSCs (N = 4 per group; p=0.0007 for Ki67, p<0.0001 for BrdU experiment; Figure 6B), suggesting that the dramatic decrease in the NSC population in mice lacking Dll1 might be due to increased cycling and S-phase entry, as observed in Lfng−/+ mice.
claims.evidence: Quantification of cell cycle markers in Dll1 knockout, leading to inference about mechanism.

claims.claim: No difference in the amount of NSCs is observed between wild-type and Jag1−/+ mice (p=0.1663).
claims.source: Interestingly, no difference in the amount of NSCs was observed between wild-type and Jag1−/+ mice (N = 4 per group; p=0.1663; Figure 6A), but there was an upward trend in the proportion of BrdU+ NSCs (N = 4 per group; p=0.8393; Figure 6B, middle panel).
claims.evidence: Quantification showing no change in total NSC numbers in Jag1 knockout.

claims.claim: There is a significant increase in Ki67+ NSCs lacking Jag1 (p<0.0001).
claims.source: There was, however, a significant increase in Ki67+ NSCs lacking Jag1 (N = 4 per group, p<0.0001; Figure 6B, left panel), suggesting that these NSCs may have a prolonged cell cycle.
claims.evidence: Quantification of cycling NSCs in Jag1 knockout, leading to inference about cell cycle duration.

claims.claim: The ratio of BrdU+ NSCs is significantly higher in iJag1fl/fl mice compared to controls (p=0.0028).
claims.source: In these conditional homozygous knockout mice (iJag1fl/fl), the ratio of BrdU+ mutant NSCs was significantly higher than in controls (Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT; N = 4 per group, p=0.0028; Figure 6B, right panel).
claims.evidence: Quantification of S-phase entry in conditional Jag1 knockout.

claims.claim: The number of CldU/IdU double-labeled NSCs in both Jag1−/+ and iJag1fl/fl mice is notably higher than controls at both 3 and 7 days (p=0.0164 at 3d, p=0.0016 at 7d; p=0.0003 for iJag1fl/fl mice).
claims.source: The number of CldU/IdU double-labeled NSCs in both Jag1−/+ and iJag1fl/fl mice was notably higher than controls at both 3 and 7 days (N = 4 per group, p=0.0164 at 3d, p=0.0016 at 7d; p=0.0003 for iJag1fl/fl mice; Figure 6C) and accompanied by a greater proportion of CldU+ Ki67+ NSCs (N = 4 per group; p=0.005 for wild-type vs Jag1−/+; Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: Sequential thymidine analog labeling showing increased cell cycle re-entry in Jag1 mutants.

claims.claim: There is a greater proportion of CldU+ Ki67+ NSCs in Jag1−/+ mice compared to wild-type (p=0.005).
claims.source: The number of CldU/IdU double-labeled NSCs in both Jag1−/+ and iJag1fl/fl mice was notably higher than controls at both 3 and 7 days (N = 4 per group, p=0.0164 at 3d, p=0.0016 at 7d; p=0.0003 for iJag1fl/fl mice; Figure 6C) and accompanied by a greater proportion of CldU+ Ki67+ NSCs (N = 4 per group; p=0.005 for wild-type vs Jag1−/+; Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: Quantification of cycling NSCs retaining label in Jag1 knockout.

claims.claim: NICD1 expression is higher in individual mutant NSC clones in iJag1fl/fl mice two weeks after induction compared to controls.
claims.source: The increase in NICD1 expression in individual mutant NSC clones in iJag1fl/fl mice two weeks after induction (Figure 6E) supports this notion, in agreement with the reported conditional overexpression of NICD1, which increases cell cycle re-entry of NSCs (Breunig et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: Quantification of NICD1 intensity in Jag1 mutant NSCs, supported by citation.

claims.claim: There is no difference in double-labeled NSCs between Dll1−/+ and wild-type mice at 3 days (p=0.9624), but at 7 days no CldU/IdU double-positive cells can be detected (p=0.0016).
claims.source: Conversely, there was no difference in double-labeled NSCs between Dll1−/+ and wild-type mice at 3 days, but at 7 days no CldU/IdU double-positive cells could be detected, suggesting that NSCs did not re-enter cell cycle (N = 4 per group, p=0.9624 at 3d, p=0.0016 at 7d; Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Sequential thymidine analog labeling showing lack of cell cycle re-entry in Dll1 mutants, leading to inference.

claims.claim: In the absence of Dll1, none of the BrdU+ NSCs two hours following a single BrdU injection retain BrdU at 7 days.
claims.source: In the absence of Dll1, none of the BrdU+ NSCs two hours following a single BrdU injection retained BrdU at 7 days (N = 4; Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: BrdU retention assay showing complete loss of label in Dll1 mutant NSCs.

claims.claim: Dll1−/+ mice have significantly more S100β+ astrocytes among BrdU+ cells 30 days after BrdU injection (p=0.016).
claims.source: To determine the fate of NSCs in Dll1−/+ mice, we injected BrdU and sacrificed the animals 30 days later. We observed significantly more S100β+ astrocytes among the BrdU+ cells. Thus, as in Lfng−/+, more Dll1 mutant NSCs terminally differentiate into astrocytes (N = 4 per group, p=0.016; Figure 6H).
claims.evidence: BrdU fate mapping showing increased astrocytic differentiation in Dll1 mutants.

claims.claim: The number of BrdU retaining NSCs in Jag1−/+ mice is much greater 7 days following the BrdU pulse (1.6 fold, p=0.0028) than two hours after the pulse.
claims.source: The findings were opposite in mice lacking Jag1: the number of BrdU retaining NSCs was much greater 7 days following the BrdU pulse (1.6 fold, p=0.0028) than two hours after the pulse (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: BrdU retention assay showing increased label retention in Jag1 mutants, suggesting self-renewal.

claims.claim: The number of tdTomato+ NSCs markedly increases at both 7 and 30 days in iJag1fl/fl mutant mice compared to control mice (p=0.0263 and p<0.0001 for NSC at 7d and 30d).
claims.source: Initially, both control and mutant mice had a similar number of tdTomato+ NSCs and ANPs, but this number markedly increased at both 7 and 30 days in mutant compared to control mice (N = 4 per group, p=0.0263 and p<0.0001 for NSC at 7d and 30d, p=0.0033 and p=0.069 for ANP at 7d and 30d; Figure 6I).
claims.evidence: Longitudinal quantification showing NSC accumulation in Jag1 conditional knockout.

claims.claim: The number of tdTomato+ ANPs increases at 7 days (p=0.0033) in iJag1fl/fl mutant mice compared to control mice.
claims.source: Initially, both control and mutant mice had a similar number of tdTomato+ NSCs and ANPs, but this number markedly increased at both 7 and 30 days in mutant compared to control mice (N = 4 per group, p=0.0263 and p<0.0001 for NSC at 7d and 30d, p=0.0033 and p=0.069 for ANP at 7d and 30d; Figure 6I).
claims.evidence: Longitudinal quantification showing ANP accumulation in Jag1 conditional knockout.

claims.claim: Both the number of Type 2a ANPs and the size of the ANP clusters are significantly greater in Jag1−/+ mice than controls.
claims.source: Indeed, both the number of Type 2a ANPs and the size of the ANP clusters were significantly greater in Jag1−/+ mice than controls (Figure 6G).
claims.evidence: Quantification of ANP numbers and cluster sizes in Jag1 knockout.

claims.claim: iJag1fl/fl mice have a prominent decrease in the number of apoptotic cells compared to wild-type.
claims.source: To determine whether apoptosis had any role in the increased number of ANPs in Jag1 mutants, we quantified the number of apoptotic cells using activated caspase-3 staining and ApopTag. Both methods demonstrated a prominent decrease in the number of apoptotic cells in iJag1fl/fl mice compared to wild-type (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Apoptosis detection assays showing reduced cell death in Jag1 mutants.

claims.claim: Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+ double knockout mice have far fewer NSCs than wild-type (p<0.0001).
claims.source: Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+ double knockout mice had far fewer NSCs than wild-type (N = 3 for Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+ and N = 4 controls; p<0.0001 for wild-type vs Lfng−/+ and Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+), but did not differ significantly from Lfng−/+ mice (N = 3 for Lfng−/+, p=0.6869 for Lfng−/+ vs Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: Quantification of NSC numbers in double knockout mice.

claims.claim: Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+ double knockout mice show a higher BrdU+ NSC ratio than wild-type (p=0.0003).
claims.source: The double knockout showed a higher BrdU+ NSC ratio than wild-type (N = 3; p=0.0001 for wild-type vs Lfng−/+, p=0.0003 for wild-type vs Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+, p=0.6724 for Lfng−/+ vs Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+; Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), similar to Lfng−/+ mice.
claims.evidence: Quantification of S-phase entry in double knockout mice.

claims.claim: Greater NSC cell cycle re-entry is observed in Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+ double knockout mice (p<0.00001).
claims.source: Finally, we observed greater NSC cell cycle re-entry in double knockout mice (N = 3; p<0.00001 for wild-type vs Lfng-/+; Jag1−/+ and Lfng−/+ vs Lfng−/+; Jag1−/+), suggesting that removal of Jag1 can reverse the low cell cycle re-entry phenotype observed in the NSCs lacking Lfng (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: Sequential thymidine analog labeling in double knockout showing epistatic relationship.

claims.claim: Lfng glycosylation of Notch does not affect Jag1 binding, but the NICD is not cleaved from the Jag1-Notch complex.
claims.source: In the Notch signal-receiving NSC, Lfng glycosylation of the Notch receptor potentiates Notch signaling from Dll1 and attenuates signaling from Jag1: even though Lfng glycosylation of Notch does not affect Jag1 binding, the NICD is not cleaved from the Jag1-Notch complex.
claims.evidence: Mechanistic explanation based on established knowledge of Lfng function.

claims.claim: Lfng modification of Notch elevates NICD production upon Dll1 binding.
claims.source: Lfng N-glycosylates Notch receptors (Moloney et al., 2000), affecting the intracellular cleavage of the heterodimeric receptor complex and generation of the NICD following ligand binding: typically, Lfng modification of Notch elevates NICD production upon Dll1 binding, but decreases it following engagement to Jag1 (Haines and Irvine, 2003; LeBon et al., 2014; Stanley and Okajima, 2010; Taylor et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: Mechanistic explanation supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: Lfng modification of Notch decreases NICD production following engagement to Jag1.
claims.source: Lfng N-glycosylates Notch receptors (Moloney et al., 2000), affecting the intracellular cleavage of the heterodimeric receptor complex and generation of the NICD following ligand binding: typically, Lfng modification of Notch elevates NICD production upon Dll1 binding, but decreases it following engagement to Jag1 (Haines and Irvine, 2003; LeBon et al., 2014; Stanley and Okajima, 2010; Taylor et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: Mechanistic explanation supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: Notch signaling plays a key role in the balance between quiescence and activation of hippocampal neural stem cells.
claims.source: Hippocampal neural stem cells (NSCs) integrate inputs from multiple sources to balance quiescence and activation. Notch signaling plays a key role during this process.
claims.evidence: Summary statement in abstract supported by experimental data throughout manuscript.

claims.claim: Lunatic fringe (Lfng) is selectively expressed in NSCs.
claims.source: Here, we report that Lunatic fringe (Lfng), a key modifier of the Notch receptor, is selectively expressed in NSCs.
claims.evidence: Summary statement in abstract supported by expression data throughout manuscript.

claims.claim: Lfng in NSCs and Notch ligands Delta1 and Jagged1, expressed by their progeny, together influence NSC recruitment, cell cycle duration, and terminal fate.
claims.source: Further, Lfng in NSCs and Notch ligands Delta1 and Jagged1, expressed by their progeny, together influence NSC recruitment, cell cycle duration, and terminal fate.
claims.evidence: Summary statement in abstract supported by loss-of-function experiments throughout manuscript.

claims.claim: Lfng-mediated Notch signaling enables direct communication between a NSC and its descendants, so that progeny can send feedback signals to the 'mother' cell to modify its cell cycle status.
claims.source: We propose a new model in which Lfng-mediated Notch signaling enables direct communication between a NSC and its descendants, so that progeny can send feedback signals to the 'mother' cell to modify its cell cycle status.
claims.evidence: Model proposed based on integration of expression patterns and loss-of-function data.

claims.claim: Nearly 80% of the newborn progeny of NSCs die by apoptosis.
claims.source: Taking into account that nearly 80% of the newborn progeny of NSCs die by apoptosis (Sierra et al., 2010), the neurogenic niche needs to ensure not only that it responds properly to stimuli but also that NSCs, once they are activated, are cycling enough to produce sufficient progeny.
claims.evidence: Statement supported by citation to published work.

claims.claim: Communication between 'mother' and 'daughter' cells is known to regulate lateral inhibition in the vertebral neural tube.
claims.source: Communication between 'mother' and 'daughter' cells is known to regulate lateral inhibition in the vertebral neural tube (Nikolaou et al., 2009) and Drosophila oocytes (Zhao et al., 2000), and it occurs during angiogenesis (Benedito et al., 2009) and oncogenesis (Xu et al., 2012); in each case this communication involves Notch signaling (Haines and Irvine, 2003; LeBon et al., 2014; Stanley and Okajima, 2010; Taylor et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: Statement supported by multiple citations to published work.

claims.claim: In the fetal brain, Notch activity maintains embryonic NSCs in an undifferentiated state by suppressing pro-neural gene expression.
claims.source: In the fetal brain, Notch activity maintains embryonic NSCs in an undifferentiated state (Louvi and Artavanis-Tsakonas, 2006) by suppressing pro-neural gene expression (Gaiano et al., 2000; Ishibashi et al., 1994; Lütolf et al., 2002) and supporting progenitor survival (Androutsellis-Theotokis et al., 2006; Louvi and Artavanis-Tsakonas, 2006).
claims.evidence: Statement about developmental role of Notch supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: In the adult brain, Notch influences quiescence, cycling, and exit of neuroprogenitors from the cell cycle, acting most likely in a cell-autonomous fashion.
claims.source: In the adult brain, Notch seems to influence quiescence, cycling, and exit of neuroprogenitors from the cell cycle, acting most likely in a cell-autonomous fashion (Ables et al., 2010; Basak et al., 2012; Breunig et al., 2007; Ehm et al., 2010; Ehret et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: Statement about adult Notch function supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: Glycosylation of Notch receptors by fringe proteins affects the intracellular cleavage of the heterodimeric receptor complex and generation of NICD following ligand binding.
claims.source: Glycosylation of Notch receptors by fringe proteins affects the intracellular cleavage of the heterodimeric receptor complex and generation of the Notch1 Intra Cellular Domain (NICD) following ligand binding.
claims.evidence: Mechanistic explanation based on established knowledge of fringe function.

claims.claim: NICD production typically increases upon binding by Delta-like (Dll) and decreases following Jagged1 (Jag1) binding.
claims.source: Typically, NICD production increases upon binding by Delta-like (Dll) and decreases following Jagged1 (Jag1) binding (LeBon et al., 2014; Stanley and Okajima, 2010; Taylor et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2005); differential Notch cleavage ensures varying expression of downstream cell cycle genes (Chapouton et al., 2010; Isomura and Kageyama, 2014; Nellemann et al., 2001; Ninov et al., 2012; Yoshiura et al., 2007).

results.result: Lfng-eGFP is selectively expressed in adult hippocampal neural stem cells (NSCs) in the subgranular zone of the dentate gyrus. The reporter accurately recapitulates endogenous Lfng expression and co-localizes with established NSC markers (Nestin, Sox2, Vimentin, GFAP), with 81.7±2.6% of eGFP+ cells being NSCs.
results.evaluation: Multiple independent lines of evidence converge to support NSC-specific expression: spatial restriction to SGZ (C1), characteristic NSC morphology (C2), validation by in situ hybridization (C3), co-localization with β-Gal in genetic cross (C4), co-expression with known NSC markers (C5), and quantitative stereological analysis (C11). The data are internally consistent and use appropriate controls.

results.result: Lfng-eGFP expression is rapidly cleared from amplifying neuroprogenitors (ANPs) and is not detected in differentiated cell types. Only 10% of Type 2a ANPs and no Type 2b ANPs express eGFP, with clearance occurring between days 1-3 post-BrdU injection, consistent with GFP protein half-life.
results.evaluation: The temporal dynamics of eGFP clearance (C6) correlate with known GFP half-life (C7), and quantitative analysis shows minimal expression in ANPs (C8, C9) and absence in differentiated cells (C10). The comparison with Nestin-GFP mice provides an appropriate control demonstrating the specificity of Lfng-eGFP for NSCs versus broader progenitor populations.

results.result: Lfng-eGFP+ cells exhibit functional properties of quiescent NSCs that can be activated by physiological and pathological stimuli. Only 15.0±3.0% of eGFP+ cells are lost following temozolomide treatment (versus 35.0±4.0% in Nestin-GFP mice), and both electroconvulsive shock and physical exercise significantly increase BrdU incorporation in Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs.
results.evaluation: The resistance to temozolomide (C13, C14) is consistent with quiescent cell properties, and the activation by ECS (C15, p=0.0006) and physical exercise (C16, p=0.0271) demonstrates functional plasticity. The comparison with Nestin-GFP mice provides appropriate controls showing that Lfng-eGFP labels a more quiescent population.

results.result: Lfng-eGFP maintains specificity for NSCs during aging, unlike Nestin-GFP which increasingly labels non-neuroprogenitors in older mice. Both reporters show comparable decline in NSC numbers over 18 months, but Lfng-eGFP selectivity remains stable (p>0.15 at all timepoints).
results.evaluation: The longitudinal analysis (C17, C18) demonstrates that both reporters track NSC decline similarly, but the differential specificity during aging (C19, C20) establishes Lfng-eGFP as superior for aging studies. Statistical analysis with appropriate post-hoc tests supports the claims. This validates the utility of the model across the lifespan.

results.result: The Lfng-CreERT2 mouse line enables specific genetic manipulation of NSCs. Following tamoxifen induction, 89.1±4.0% of tdTomato+ cells are eGFP+ NSCs, with no leaky expression in vehicle controls. Diphtheria toxin-mediated ablation of Lfng-CreERT2+ cells reduces NSCs by 36.8±1.5% and Ki67+ cells by 57.3±2.4%.
results.evaluation: The co-localization data (C21, C22) demonstrate specificity of the CreERT2 line, the vehicle control (C23) confirms no leakiness, and the ablation experiment (C24, C25) functionally validates that targeted cells are proliferative NSCs. The convergence of multiple validation approaches strongly supports the utility of this new genetic tool.

results.result: Lineage tracing with Lfng-CreERT2;RCL-tdT mice demonstrates that Lfng-expressing NSCs undergo both symmetric and asymmetric division and generate diverse progeny including neurons and astrocytes. The temporal progression shows Type 2b ANPs at 3 days, immature neurons at 7 days, and mature NeuN+ granule cells at 30 days, with granule cells representing ~30% of tdTomato+ cells at 60 days.
results.evaluation: The lineage tracing data provide comprehensive temporal characterization of NSC progeny (C26-C34). The observation of both division modes (C26), the sequential appearance of cell types (C27-C29), and the quantitative fate mapping (C32-C34) are internally consistent and follow expected developmental timelines. The detection of astrocytic progeny (C30, C31) adds to the multipotency evidence.

results.result: Key Notch pathway components are spatially organized in the SGZ niche: Notch1 is expressed on NSC surfaces, Jag1 on presumed ANPs surrounding NSCs, and Dll1 on granule neurons neighboring NSC soma. Hes5, a canonical Notch target, is present in some but not all Lfng-eGFP+ NSCs.
results.evaluation: The immunohistochemistry data (C35-C37) are supported by citations to prior work and show appropriate spatial organization of ligands and receptors. The heterogeneous Hes5 expression (C38) is consistent with dynamic Notch signaling and provides context for subsequent functional studies. The data establish the molecular framework for the proposed model.

results.result: Notch signaling activity, measured by CBF:H2B-Venus reporter and NICD1 expression, is present in approximately half of NSCs, declines during differentiation through ANPs and neuroblasts, and reactivates in mature granule neurons. Over 90% of Venus+ cells in SGZ and 95% in GZ co-express NICD1, validating NICD1 as a reliable marker of Notch activity.
results.evaluation: The Venus reporter data (C39-C41) show dynamic Notch activity across cell types, and the high co-localization with NICD1 (C42, C43) validates the use of NICD1 for subsequent intensity measurements. The pattern of Notch activity (high in NSCs, low during differentiation, reactivated in mature neurons) is consistent with prior literature and provides functional context for the pathway.

results.result: Loss of Lfng causes NSC depletion through increased cell cycle entry. Lfng-/+ mice have markedly fewer NSCs with significantly higher proportions of Ki67+ (p=0.0221) and BrdU+ (p=0.0017) NSCs. Conditional knockout (iLfngfl/fl) shows cell-autonomous effects with reduced NICD1 intensity, and the hyperactivation phenotype persists under ECS stimulation (p=0.0178).
results.evaluation: The convergence of constitutive knockout (C44-C46, C49), conditional knockout (C47, C50), and the demonstration of cell autonomy (C48) provide strong evidence for Lfng's role in maintaining NSC quiescence. The reduced NICD1 intensity (C50) provides a mechanistic link to Notch signaling. The dose-dependent effects and multiple experimental approaches strengthen the conclusions.

results.result: Lfng mutant NSCs show impaired cell cycle re-entry and rapid loss of BrdU label. No double-labeled (CldU/IdU) NSCs are found in iLfngfl/fl mice, and only 5.2% of BrdU+ NSCs retain label at 7 days (versus 92.4% in controls, p=0.0003). Decreased CldU/Ki67 double-labeling (p=0.0105) and reduced apoptosis in mutants suggest alternative fates rather than cell death.
results.evaluation: The sequential thymidine analog labeling (C51, C52) and BrdU retention assays (C53, C54) provide complementary evidence for altered cell cycle dynamics. The reduced apoptosis (C55) rules out cell death as the primary mechanism of NSC loss, supporting the authors' interpretation that mutant NSCs exit the cycle or differentiate. The data are internally consistent and use appropriate controls.

results.result: Conditional deletion of Lfng leads to reduced ANP production and accelerated differentiation into astrocyte-like cells. The number of mutant ANPs significantly declines at 7 and 30 days (p=0.0024, p=0.0049), while tdTomato+ astrocyte-like cells increase (p=0.0003, p<0.0001). BrdU-retaining astrocyte-like cells are elevated at 7 days (p=0.0302) but not 30 days (p=0.4412), suggesting rapid differentiation.
results.evaluation: The longitudinal quantification (C56-C58) shows coordinated changes in cell populations consistent with altered differentiation. The temporal dynamics of BrdU retention in astrocyte-like cells (C59) support the interpretation of accelerated differentiation rather than simple accumulation. The data provide mechanistic insight into how Lfng loss depletes the NSC pool.

results.result: Loss of Dll1 causes severe NSC depletion through increased cycling, impaired cell cycle re-entry, and enhanced astrocytic differentiation. Dll1-/+ mice have far fewer NSCs than wild-type or Jag1-/+ mice, with increased Ki67+ (p=0.0007) and BrdU+ (p<0.0001) NSCs. No CldU/IdU double-positive NSCs are detected at 7 days (p=0.0016), no BrdU retention occurs, and significantly more S100β+ astrocytes are generated (p=0.016).
results.evaluation: The data show a coherent phenotype: increased initial activation (C61), failure to re-enter cell cycle (C68), complete loss of BrdU label (C69), and terminal astrocytic differentiation (C70). The comparison with Jag1-/+ mice (C60) demonstrates ligand-specific effects. The phenotypic similarity to Lfng mutants supports the proposed model of Dll1-Lfng-Notch signaling maintaining NSC quiescence.

results.result: Loss of Jag1 does not reduce total NSC numbers but increases cell cycle duration and re-entry. Jag1-/+ mice show no difference in NSC numbers (p=0.1663) but have significantly more Ki67+ NSCs (p<0.0001). Conditional knockout (iJag1fl/fl) shows increased BrdU+ NSCs (p=0.0028), more CldU/IdU double-labeled NSCs at 3 and 7 days (p=0.0164, p=0.0016), and elevated NICD1 expression.
results.evaluation: The data demonstrate that Jag1 loss has opposite effects to Dll1 loss: NSCs are maintained (C62) but cycle longer (C63, C66) and re-enter more frequently (C65). The increased NICD1 in mutant NSCs (C67) provides mechanistic support. The comparison between constitutive heterozygous and conditional homozygous knockouts (C64) suggests dose-dependent effects on cell cycle entry versus duration.

results.result: Jag1 mutant NSCs show increased self-renewal and ANP production. BrdU-retaining NSCs increase 1.6-fold at 7 days (p=0.0028), tdTomato+ NSCs accumulate at 7 and 30 days (p=0.0263, p<0.0001), and tdTomato+ ANPs increase at 7 days (p=0.0033). Type 2a ANPs and cluster sizes are significantly greater in Jag1-/+ mice, with reduced apoptosis in iJag1fl/fl mice.
results.evaluation: The BrdU retention data (C71) suggest self-renewal, supported by NSC accumulation in lineage tracing (C72). The increased ANP production (C73, C74) and reduced apoptosis (C75) are consistent with prolonged NSC cycling. The data support the model that Jag1 normally limits NSC division, and its removal leads to expanded progenitor pools.

results.result: Lfng-/+; Jag1-/+ double knockout mice phenocopy Lfng-/+ mice in NSC number and BrdU incorporation but show increased cell cycle re-entry (p<0.00001), suggesting that Jag1 removal can reverse the impaired re-entry phenotype of Lfng mutants while not rescuing NSC depletion.
results.evaluation: The double knockout analysis (C76-C78) provides genetic epistasis data supporting the model. The similarity to Lfng-/+ in NSC numbers (C76) and BrdU incorporation (C77) indicates Lfng acts upstream or in parallel to Jag1 for NSC recruitment. The rescue of cell cycle re-entry (C78) demonstrates that Jag1 specifically regulates this aspect downstream of or independently from Lfng's role in recruitment.

results.result: The authors propose a model where Lfng-mediated Notch signaling enables feedback communication between NSCs and their progeny to regulate NSC quiescence and activation. Lfng in NSCs modulates Notch receptor sensitivity to differentially respond to Dll1 (from granule cells, promoting quiescence) versus Jag1 (from ANPs, promoting cell cycle exit), thereby preserving the NSC pool.
results.evaluation: The model (C85) integrates the selective expression of Lfng in NSCs (C83), the spatial organization of ligands (C35-C37), and the opposing effects of Dll1 and Jag1 loss-of-function (C60-C75). The mechanistic basis (C79-C81) is supported by established literature on Lfng function. While the model is partly speculative, it is well-supported by the comprehensive genetic and cellular data presented and provides a unifying framework for the observations.

results.result: The manuscript contextualizes the findings within established knowledge of neurogenesis, Notch signaling, and mother-daughter cell communication. Prior work shows ~80% of newborn NSC progeny die by apoptosis, mother-daughter communication occurs in other systems via Notch, and Notch maintains embryonic NSCs while influencing adult NSC quiescence and cycling.
results.evaluation: These claims (C86-C90) appropriately cite relevant literature to establish context and justify the study's rationale. The citations appear accurate and relevant to the claims made. This background supports the novelty and significance of investigating Lfng-mediated Notch signaling in adult hippocampal NSCs.

results.result: The manuscript establishes the mechanistic basis for Lfng function: fringe proteins glycosylate Notch receptors, affecting NICD generation following ligand binding. NICD production typically increases with Dll binding and decreases with Jag1 binding, leading to differential expression of downstream cell cycle genes.
results.evaluation: These mechanistic claims (C91-C93) are well-supported by multiple citations to established literature. The authors appropriately use this established knowledge as the foundation for their hypothesis about Lfng function in NSCs. The mechanism is consistent with the experimental observations in the manuscript.
